title: Minethings (2)
author: Upset_Ad_2549
selftext:
It is a long story, but the gist is this: in 2020 an internet game I played for a long time (it launched in 2009) shut down, and the owner gave their code to me, as a very active player who knew a bit about code, to see if I could get it working again.  

  
The game was called minethings, [www.minethings.com](http://www.minethings.com) 

The code was 11 year's old at the time, and used a PHP framwork called Cake. Anyone remember that framework? Me neither.

I had a go at resurrecting the code and within a few days realised the job was way to big for me to do in my spare time. 

  
Then along came generative AI. I've now got the code working again and added a whole bunch of functionality that I had long wished to be in the original game. [www.minethings2.com](http://www.minethings2.com) was launched a few weeks ago, and we've had 50 people signing on, about 5 of which are old players from the original game. 

That's a little bit of web history resurrected. [https://www.minethings2.com/history](https://www.minethings2.com/history) 

  
Is anyone else bringing back old games with AI? How far do you go to improve them and how faithful to the original player base do you stay? Should we be using AI exclusively to bring new games to life instead?

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body: These AI generated websites suck.  I think your project is cool, but fucking fuck that page makes my eyes bleed.  It's just so messy.  There's way too many headings and big blurbs and stuff.  It's like it's supposed to excite me but it just makes my eyes glaze over and it all reads like slop.  What ever happened to a simple legible website?
